feasibility.verdict: Largely feasible: precipitation partitioning into runoff, ET, and recharge is a core ELM diagnostic and can be quantified per column and aggregated across the elevation gradient. SWE and runoff/streamflow timing and water-table depth can be validated against SNOTEL, USGS gauges, and USGS wells. ET cannot be directly validated (no flux towers) and is constrained only via water-balance closure.
answerable: Long-term and seasonal partitioning of P into surface/subsurface runoff, ET, and recharge for each representative column
Elevation- and soil-texture-driven differences in the water balance across the sub-watershed
Validation of simulated SWE accumulation/melt against 6 SNOTEL stations
Validation of runoff timing/magnitude against USGS stream gauge daily records (where available)
Validation of simulated water-table depth (ZWT) against USGS well WTD observations
Recharge estimation via QCHARGE / subsurface drainage terms
not_answerable: Direct validation of latent-heat/ET fluxes (no flux towers in domain)
Fully distributed, routed streamflow at any specific gauge (single-column ELM has no lateral routing; runoff is point-scale)
Sub-watershed spatial recharge maps beyond the representative-column archetype

parsed.n_justification: The dominant controls are elevation (352-1977 m, driving orographic precipitation and snow/rain partitioning), soil texture, and forcing. Six columns are chosen to co-locate with the 6 available SNOTEL stations so SWE validation is one-to-one, while spanning the elevation gradient (valley/rain-dominated to alpine/snow-dominated) and sampling contrasting soil textures. This is sufficient to characterize gradient-driven partitioning without over-fitting given sparse point observations.
requires_capabilities: ELM single-column (PTS_MODE) simulation with GSWP3/CLMNCEP-style forcing 1980-2018
Model spin-up (accelerated/AD + final spin-up) prior to the 39-year transient to equilibrate soil moisture and groundwater store
Site-specific surface datasets (soil texture, PFT) per column
PFLOTRAN coupling (ELM-PFLOTRAN) optional for higher-fidelity variably-saturated recharge/water-table dynamics validated against USGS wells
Post-processing for annual/seasonal water-balance closure and comparison to SNOTEL SWE, USGS gauges, USGS well WTD
assumptions: Recharge is approximated by ELM QCHARGE (gravity drainage to the unconfined aquifer) plus QDRAI where applicable; ΔSWE and ΔsoilΔWA storage changes are accounted for in closure.
Single-column runoff (QRUNOFF) is point-scale and unrouted; validation against stream gauges is on seasonal fractions/timing, not absolute routed discharge.
SNOTEL station coordinates are used as approximate column locations; exact elevations set from station metadata via surface-data override.
ET is unvalidated directly (no flux towers) and is assessed only through water-balance consistency and reasonableness vs. regional literature.
Forcing is downscaled/elevation-corrected where possible; orographic precipitation gradient is represented by column placement across elevation bands.
First ~5-10 years of the transient may be treated as additional spin-up and excluded from long-term partitioning statistics.
